correctness.rationale: For every finite abelian A and nongenerating d, the quotient A/<d> labels exactly g² unique edge-disjoint two-dimensional pieces meeting only at vertices. A coordinate relabeling makes each piece the cyclic 0/1 two-level complex on h symbols, with every vertex link a 2h-cycle and paired opposite triangular orientations. Euler characteristic determines genus (h−1)(h−2)/2. A connected bipartite surface–vertex incidence graph has g²+3q nodes and 3gq edges, hence cycle rank (g−1)(3q−g−1). The explicit graph-of-spaces homotopy argument supplies the full wedge, integral torsion-freeness and the Betti identities. The actual standalone verifier passed 42 nonunit cases plus controls, including signed modular boundaries in two characteristics, without extrapolating the finite tests into a proof.

value.rationale: The earlier exact two-level Latin computation explicitly leaves nongenerating differences unresolved, making this a motivated structural boundary rather than a cosmetic parameter change. A single fixed face vector hides distinct surface genera, singular links and free homology ranks; for q=6 a generating difference yields one genus-ten surface, whereas d=2 gives four tori plus fifteen circles and d=3 gives nine spheres plus twenty-eight circles. The theorem fully classifies an infinite group family and preserves nontrivial surface fundamental groups, so the new precise homotopy invariant is useful beyond the Euler-characteristic and homology ranks alone.
